facts.text: Conversion copywriting and voice-of-customer (VOC) research. Not prose craft - evidence gathering and message strategy for the copywriter or PM before the prose gets written. Covers VOC research sources (customer reviews, support tickets, sales-call transcripts, Reddit and community threads, G2/Trustpilot, exit surveys); the they-say/we-say gap analysis (how customers describe the problem vs how the marketing team describes it); Jobs-to-be-Done message extraction (functional, emotional, and social JTBD from customer language); building a message hierarchy (primary claim, proof, objection handlers); post-purchase and "what almost stopped you" surveys to surface objection inventories; hypothesis-driven copy testing (what to A/B test - headline, value prop, CTA, lead, hero image - and why); Eugene Schwartz stages of awareness applied to VOC; the HiPPO ("highest-paid person's opinion") problem in copy decisions. Route prose framework questions (AIDA, PAS, CTA wording) to content-and-marketing-writing; A/B test statistics to da-analytical-methods; persuasion theory to applied-psychology.
Before writing any new landing page, ad, or email, when the team's internal language for a problem doesn't match how customers actually describe it in their own words.

facts.text: Building a message hierarchy for a launch or campaign where the primary claim, its proof, and the objections it needs to preempt all need to trace back to real customer evidence.

facts.text: Diagnosing why existing copy underperforms by checking whether it's still targeting an earlier Schwartz awareness stage than the actual audience has reached.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Pull raw customer language from reviews, support tickets, sales-call transcripts, and community threads such as Reddit, G2, and Trustpilot, and quote it directly rather than paraphrasing, to preserve the they-say voice.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Run a they-say/we-say gap analysis by placing the company's internal description of the problem next to the customer's own words side by side, and rewrite toward the customer's phrasing where they diverge.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Send a post-purchase what-almost-stopped-you survey to build an objection inventory the message hierarchy's proof and objection-handler sections can directly answer.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Extract functional, emotional, and social Jobs-to-be-Done from customer language separately, since a message that only answers the functional job often misses the emotional or social reason someone actually converts.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Skipping VOC research and writing copy from internal assumptions about what customers want, which is exactly the they-say/we-say gap this discipline exists to close.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Letting the highest-paid person's opinion override customer-language evidence when deciding what to test or ship, defeating the purpose of gathering the evidence in the first place.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Treating VOC research as a one-time exercise instead of an ongoing input, when customer language and the objections customers raise shift as the product and market evolve.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Confusing this discipline with prose-writing craft itself — VOC research supplies the evidence and message strategy, but frameworks like AIDA or PAS and sentence-level writing are a separate step.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: VOC research surfaces what customers say, not necessarily what statistically drives conversion — a hypothesis generated this way still needs an actual A/B test to confirm it moves the metric.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Sources like reviews and support tickets are self-selected, which can skew toward the most satisfied or most frustrated customers rather than the median buyer.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: A message hierarchy built from VOC evidence for one audience segment or awareness stage may not transfer cleanly to a different segment or a more or less sophisticated market.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: This discipline explicitly does not cover the statistics of interpreting an A/B test result or the underlying persuasion theory — those live in separate, dedicated references.
